the TWA is an appropriate theory to use with this population.
the present findings support the generalizability of the theory of Work Adjustment to economically distressed African Americans.

the present study's results are consistent with the cultural critiques of the theory of Work Adjustment (TWA) and provide support for the moderated mediation model of the TWA with economically distressed African American employees.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TWA is a useful model to understand how African Americans make work-related decisions, and the model can be further extended by incorporating racial climate into the theory.

we have demonstrated the importance of the P-O fit and its relation to job satisfaction and turnover intentions for African American employees, and the importance of racial climate as a moderator of the P-O model.
the TWA is a useful framework for understanding the job attitudes and intentions of financially distressed African American workers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TWA can be extended and applied to economically distressed African Americans in the workplace, and that the TWA's postulates can be supported in this group of workers.
African American employees who perceive a positive racial climate at work will experience greater person-organization fit, greater job satisfaction, and lower turnover intentions.
counselors should consider the role of racial climate in their career counseling interventions with economically distressed African American clients.
